subject: Request: High-Availability Rider & Order Form Language for Atlas
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@atlasins.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlasins.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request for high-availability rider and order form language

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Atlas is excited about Redwood’s latency profile. Procurement asked me to reach out with a formal request: we need a short addendum (rider) to the MSA that captures a few specific commitments for our enterprise order form. Key asks below: 

- Uptime target: 99.95% monthly availability for the hosted inference endpoint used in our US region.
- Latency guardrail: 95th percentile response time <= 250ms for up to 200 concurrent requests (300 token median).
- Regional failover: automatic routing to secondary region with max failover time of 3 minutes and operational runbook.
- Credits/Remedy: a clear credit schedule tied to monthly availability buckets.

Can you provide proposed language we can feed into our procurement team? We also need any evidence you can share (e.g., historical latency-percentile reports, regional failover playbook excerpt). I can circulate a redline if helpful — attaching our standard MSA redline for context.

Attachments: draft_MSA_redline.pdf (procurement redline)

Thanks,
Linda Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Atlas Insurance

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
To: Linda Park <linda@atlasins.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for high-availability rider and order form language

Linda —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline. I’ve looped in Marissa (contracts) and Neha (solutions ops) to draft the exact addendum language and pull the evidence pack. Proposed next steps:

1) Marissa to share a draft HA rider and order-form snippets that map to Atlas’s buckets.
2) Neha to attach a short evidence pack: 90-day latency percentile export, regional failover summary, and runbook excerpt.
3) I’ll coordinate internal approvals and send a single redline back for Atlas procurement to review.

We can aim for a first-pass draft by EOD tomorrow (Wed). Do you have a preferred availability window for a 30-minute call if we need to walk the credit schedule?

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: HA rider language and order-form snippet (v1)

Rohan / Neha —

Drafting a concise rider and order-form exhibit below. I kept the text prescriptive but left the credit math in a table we can populate once Atlas confirms measurement windows. Please review and flag anything the product/ops team cannot commit to.

--- BEGIN DRAFT ---
High-Availability Exhibit ("Exhibit")
1. Service Availability. Redwood shall make the Hosted Inference Endpoint available 99.95% of each monthly billing cycle for requests originating from Atlas’s contracted region (US-West).
2. Measurement Window. Availability and latency shall be measured on a rolling 30-day window and reported monthly.
3. Latency SLO. Redwood targets 95th percentile response time <= 250ms for inference requests with up to 200 concurrent sessions and median request size of 300 tokens. Performance guarantees apply to requests meeting Atlas’s normal usage patterns; requests that deviate materially may be excluded.
4. Regional Failover. In the event of a regional outage, Redwood will route traffic to a pre-configured secondary region. Failover initiation time will not exceed 3 minutes under normal conditions. Redwood will provide Atlas with a documented failover runbook upon execution.
5. Credits and Remedies. If Redwood fails to meet the Service Availability SLO for a month, Atlas will be eligible for service credit according to the following ranges: [99.95% – 99.90% -> 5% credit; 99.90% – 99.00% -> 15% credit; <99.00% -> 30% credit]. Credit calculations will be applied to the monthly invoice for the impacted service.
--- END DRAFT ---

Attachments: rohan_ha_rider_v1.docx (contains the same text with tracked-change placeholders for credit calculation and measurement definitions)

Neha — can you pull the 90-day latency export and a short failover playbook snippet (1–2 pages) and add to the evidence bundle?

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Linda Park <linda@atlasins.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlasins.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: High-Availability Rider & Order Form Language for Atlas

Rohan / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turn. The draft reads well and covers the items procurement cares about. A couple of Atlas requests before we run this to legal: 

- Measurement window: procurement prefers monthly measurement aligned to Atlas billing cycles (calendar month) rather than a rolling 30-day window. Can we update the language to "measured per calendar month"?
- Credit thresholds: procurement would like to change the middle bucket to 99.90% – 99.50% -> 10% credit.

I attached our redline with the two edits called out. If you accept those, we can route to Atlas legal and get back with a final signature path.

Attachments: atlas_reviewed_rider_redline.docx

Best,
Linda Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Atlas Insurance
